core_values.name: stewardship
core_values.desc: responsibility to care for the earth and its ecosystems

core_values.name: sustainability
core_values.desc: meeting needs without compromising future capacity

key_definitions.definition: includes ecological degradation, biodiversity loss, and systemic risk
extend to future generations and sometimes non-human nature
meeting present needs without compromising future generations
avoid serious or irreversible risks under uncertainty
those who cause harm should bear remediation costs
resources shared across groups that require stewardship and governance

assumed_principles.name: precautionary_principle
assumed_principles.desc: take action despite uncertainty to avoid catastrophic harm

assumed_principles.name: stewardship_duty
assumed_principles.desc: humans have a moral duty to care for earth

decision_rule.notes: weigh outcomes for long-term ecological survival; duties serve as side-constraints

policy_heuristics.default: acceptable to fund sustainability and internalize externalities
necessary where markets fail to price ecological harms
rapid phase-out of fossil fuels; investment in renewables
balance poverty reduction with ecological integrity

edge_cases.note: consider under severe climate threat; extreme precaution
duty of justice to displaced populations
temporary hardship may be justified to ensure planetary viability
